 Alderpersons grill Chicago election officials about glitch that caused ballot shortages 
 By Mark Rivera , Barb Markoff, Christine Tressel, and Tom Jones Tuesday, November 10, 2026 12:25AM 
 During a budget meeting at City Hall Monday, alderpersons unleashed on Chicago Board of Elections staff. WLS CHICAGO (WLS) -- During a budget meeting at City Hall Monday, alderpersons unleashed on Chicago Board of Elections staff.
 The Board of Elections described the Election Day problem as a computer glitch that caused ballot shortages in multiple areas of the city. The I-Team learned 24 out of more than 1,200 precincts were affected by the shortages. That's about 2%.
 ABC7 Chicago is now streaming 24/7. Click here to watch 
 Ald. Bill Conway, of the 34th Ward, asked the executive director of the Board of Elections, Sandra Aspera, if she thought they did a good job last Tuesday.
 "I actually feel our staff did a really good job. It was the ballot error, the coding error, a big confusion, not a confusion. It created a lot of media attention and then everyone assumed it was because of the ballot error. No, there were many reasons why we had long lines," said Aspera.

 Conway disputed Aspera's assessment saying, "I think the people of the City of Chicago would disagree with that as would many people in this chamber."
 "To have precincts, tons of precincts, do not have enough ballots, to send people away to another site, to have people sitting for hours, waiting on ballots, it's egregious," said 8th Ward Ald. Michelle Harris, chairperson of committees and rules.
 Sandra Aspera was appointed executive director of the Chicago Board of Elections about a year and a half ago but has been with the BOE for three decades.
 The Chicago Board of Elections is requesting nearly $48 million for next year's budget.
 Many alderpersons told Aspera she should have done more outreach ahead of the election so there was a better understanding of who to talk to when problems arose. The Chicago municipal election is coming up in February.
